scope: part 1 only (JWT redaction ReDoS); part 2 (redactEntry idempotency) handed to the build pipeline
reproFailure: At base: '#1400 the JWT rule stays linear on a long run of eyJ- with no dot (CWE-1333)' -> took 16282 ms (bound 500 ms); '#1400 the JWT rule stays linear when the run ends in a single dotted segment' -> took 8842 ms. Raw regex timings at base: 8 KB 7 ms, 64 KB 456 ms, 256 KB 13552 ms. After fix: 8 KB 0.2 ms, 64 KB 0.3 ms, 256 KB 1.0 ms.
assumptions: The fix preserves the old regex's match set exactly rather than switching to a plain (?<![A-Za-z0-9_-]) lookbehind, which would have stopped redacting a JWT preceded by '-' (a weakening of a security control). Equivalence is pinned by a seeded 5000-case differential test against the old regex (and was checked ad hoc on 300k random inputs, 0 differences).

A JWT glued to a word character ('xeyJ...', '_eyJ...') is still not a JWT start, as under the old \b; this PR does not widen the rule. The bare-credential rule still catches long segments in failure text.
Timing bounds of 500 ms at 256 KB leave ~500x headroom over the fixed cost (~1 ms) and fail at base by ~16x, so they are not expected to flake on slow CI runners.
